Which line of code can be used to replace the INSERT comment in order to output "hello"? class C { public $ello = 'ello'; public $c; public $m; function __construct($y) { $this->c = static function($f) { // INSERT LINE OF CODE HERE }; $this->m = function() { return "h"; }; } } $x = new C("h"); $f = $x->c; echo $f($x->m); A. return $this->m() . "ello"; B. return $f() . "ello"; C. return "h". $this->ello; D. return $y . "ello";

Which keyword should be used in the line marked with "KEYWORD" instead of "self" to make this code work as intended? abstract class Base { protected function __construct() { } public static function create() { return new self(); // KEYWORD } abstract function action(); } class Item extends Base { public function action() { echo __CLASS__; } } $item = Item::create(); $item->action(); // outputs "Item"

What is the output of the following code? class Base { protected static function whoami() { echo "Base "; } public static function whoareyou() { static::whoami(); } } class A extends Base { public static function test() { Base::whoareyou(); self::whoareyou(); parent::whoareyou(); A::whoareyou(); static::whoareyou(); } public static function whoami() { echo "A "; } } class B extends A { public static function whoami() { echo "B "; } } B::test(); A. B B B B B B. Base A Base A B C. Base B B A B D. Base B A A B

What is the output of the following code? class Test { public function __call($name, $args) { call_user_func_array(array('static', "test$name"), $args); } public function testS($l) { echo "$l,"; } } class Test2 extends Test { public function testS($l) { echo "$l,$l,"; } } $test = new Test2(); $test->S('A'); A. A, B. A,A, C. A,A,A, D. PHP Warning: call_user_func_array() expects parameter 1 to be a valid callback

What change must be made to the class for the code to work as written? class Magic { protected $v = array("a" => 1, "b" => 2, "c" => 3); public function __get($v) { return $this->v[$v]; } } $m = new Magic(); $m->d[] = 4; echo $m->d[0]; A. Nothing, this code works just fine. B. Add __set method doing $this->v[$var] = $val C. Rewrite __get as: public function __get(&$v) D. Rewrite __get as: public function &__get($v) E. How many times will the function counter() be executed in the following code? function counter($start, &$stop) { if ($stop > $start) { return; } counter($start--, ++$stop); } $start = 5; $stop = 2; counter($start, $stop); A. 3 B. 4 C. 5 D. 6
